title: Missing DB Version Table
pattern: An application service booting up and executing queries against a database instance without validating that the database's schema revision matches the application's expected revision.
why_bad: If a schema migration has failed, is incomplete, or is out of sync with the application version, the app will throw strange runtime SQL errors or, worse, silently write corrupted data, leading to transaction rollbacks and production outages [378, 379, 782, 783].
detection: An application boot sequence containing database client initialization but lacking any query to a schema metadata version table.
counterexample: Valid for schemaless document databases where the application fully handles schema-on-read parsing and defaults safely [173, 626]. Mark as `Context-dependent`.
